title: POC Check-in: VPC Connectivity & On-Prem Interop (Week 4)
summary: Week 4 sync of the Private/VPC pilot. Next pilot milestone: run a 24h stability run with adjusted MTU and NAT settings; security to review key rotation process and HSM/KMS integration notes.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-07-08 16:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Noah Kim (CSM) — Maya Lopez (Platform), Dan Cho (Security), Raj Patel (SRE), Elena Garcia (Infra)

Summary (auto): Week 4 pilot sync. Discussed intermittent TLS handshake failures across the site-to-site VPN, MTU/NAT tuning, route asymmetry, and a kernel upgrade that briefly regressed p99 latency. Agreed to a 24h stability run and concrete config deliverables.

[00:00] Liam: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, we are on the week 4 check-in for the VPC/private interop pilot, I'm Liam from Redwood — with me Priya SE and Noah CSM.
[00:08] Maya: hey thanks Liam, we have Raj and Elena and Dan on this end. we pulled the logs you asked for last run.
[00:12] Priya: great, quick agenda: 1) brief results since last week, 2) networking anomalies TLS/NAT/MTU, 3) kernel upgrade effects, 4) next steps. sound good?
[00:20] Raj: yep sounds good.
[00:22] Liam: cool, i'll hand to Priya for the metrics.
[00:25] Priya: alright so the core test we ran was the mixed-proxy workload, roughly 120 qps steady state with bursts to 400 qps. p50/p95 looked stable and matched our baseline, p99 unfortunately spiked to ~1.2s for a two hour window on 07/07 starting ~03:00 UTC. that aligned with a kernel upgrade we pushed to the test nodes, after we pushed a backout and tuned the network stack p99 dropped back to ~320ms.
[00:52] Raj: just to confirm, that kernel was 5.19.x?
[00:55] Priya: yeah 5.19.12, and we enabled the new batching kernel flags. seems like the new interrupt coalescing + GRO/LRO interplay caused occasional packetization that then triggered a TLS retry in the client stack.
[01:12] Elena: we also saw increased retransmits on the VPN side — there were NAT timeouts coinciding, so packets were getting dropped and then the handshake retried.
[01:20] Dan: when you say TLS retry, is it the client re-establishing the handshake or are we seeing half-done sessions?
[01:26] Priya: mostly full handshake restart — the server is dropping the connection mid-handshake because it never sees the final packet, likely due to MTU or intermediate NAT timeouts. transcription note: sometimes the pcap names were mis-identified as 'pack on' in the logs.
[01:40] Liam: thanks, good lead. maya can you describe your VPN topology quickly?
[01:45] Maya: sure, we have two transit gateways in different AZs, a site-to-site VPN to the on-prem datacenter, and a peering to an AWS VPC where the Redwood private nodes are mounted as ENIs via a customer-managed transit. we run a standard AWS VPN with a Cisco edge box and we do NAT on the edge and also have a managed transit gateway NAT on the cloud side.
[02:05] Priya: ok that double NAT path can increase fragmentation risk, especially if MTU defaults remain 1500 upstream but the IPSec overhead brings it lower.
[02:13] Elena: our ipsec is set to default mtu 1500, but the tunnel encapsulation reduces it to about 1380 — we didn't realize fragmentation was happening at the transit gateway.
[02:22] Priya: that matches the symptom. we recommend testing MTU values 1400, 1420, 1380 and observe; also bump NAT idle timeouts from default 120s to 300-360s for the duration of the pilot to ensure long-lived TLS sessions don't get nabbed by NAT garbage collection.
[02:43] Raj: sounds reasonable. any iptables snippets you suggest? we do have custom rules for pod egress.
[02:48] Priya: yes, i'll send a small snippet that sets the MSS clamping on the egress to prevent fragmentation, and a sample conntrack tuning set to increase NETFILTER conntrack timeout for tcp established. i'll include specific echo commands.
[03:02] Liam: great. quick aside on failover — we observed that when the private nodes were unreachable, the client app fallback to Redwood-hosted succeeded but had a 3x cost delta in tokens and slightly higher latency. want to confirm we have agreed fallback windows and budget alerts.
[03:20] Dan: can you quantify the cost delta?
[03:22] Liam: roughly 3x per token for edge-hosted fallback due to model size and request patterns, I'll send the pricing slice in the notes.
[03:29] Dan: alright we'll need that, security wants to model worst-case egress + cost.
[03:33] Noah: we'll include an example alerting policy for when failover exceeds 5% of requests per 1h window.
[03:40] Priya: circling back to the kernel upgrade — we want to recommend a phased roll with canary traffic routing and a staged rollback window; after today's discussion we suggest pausing any further kernel upgrades until after the 24h stability run.
[03:54] Maya: agreed, we can't risk a regression during core business hours.
[03:57] Raj: one question — you mentioned TLS tracing, is that at app layer or kernel?
[04:02] Priya: a mix. we can add additional telemetry in the Redwood agent to log handshake timing and capture the exact TLS alert codes, and at the kernel level we can enable extra tcpdbg on the nodes for a short window. these traces are safe but will add CPU overhead, so schedule during off-peak.
[04:20] Elena: ok can you provide the exact commands and expected overhead?
[04:24] Priya: yes i'll include that in the deliverable.
[04:27] Liam: the other networking issue we saw was route asymmetry reported by BGP on your transit gateway — packets sometimes took a different egress path causing stateful NAT to drop replies.
[04:38] Maya: yeah we noticed that at 03:05 UTC — the TGW route table entry to our on-prem subnet flipped to the other attachment and the conntrack entries didn't survive.
[04:47] Raj: looking back at logs it seems the attachment health check briefly failed and traffic moved to the secondary.
[04:54] Priya: for asymmetry, longest match routing and sticky source NAT help; we also recommended configuring the TGW route propagation to be explicit and not rely on automatic route flapping. i'll add a doc link.
[05:06] Liam: quick security point — Dan, are there constraints around enabling extra TLS logs or are you okay for short windows?
[05:12] Dan: security is generally OK as long as logs do not contain raw private keys or PII and are stored in our logging S3 with lifecycle. also we need KMS/HSM usage documented: how keys are rotated and whether Redwood ever sees plaintext keys.
[05:27] Priya: Redwood never sees plaintext private keys when HSM is enabled; we can provide the integration diagram and KMS envelope flow.
[05:33] Dan: please include whether key rotation requires downtime or if seamless rotation is supported.
[05:38] Priya: seamless rotation supported via double-encrypt handshake; i'll note the caveats.
[05:43] Maya: one operational ask — can Redwood produce a lightweight benchmark harness we can run inside our VPC to simulate the same qps shape? replicating your traffic generator was a bit tricky.
[05:54] Liam: yes we have a small harness we use internally — we'll sanitize and share a docker image + runbook. Noah to coordinate.
[06:01] Noah: will do, i'll post the link and a quick runbook in the shared Confluence. expecting low friction.
[06:06] Priya: another note: for MTU changes we prefer to validate via tcpdump and a small traceroute with -M option (mtu probing) so that you can confirm no fragmentation. we'll include the step by step.
[06:18] Raj: thanks.
[06:20] Liam: anything else on infra before we move to scheduling?
[06:23] Elena: just one more — we saw sporadic time skew on one of the on-prem boxes, ntpd drift could cause TLS replay issues. we'll sync clocks and report back.
[06:33] Priya: good catch, clock skew can definitely cause handshakes to fail if cert validity windows are tight.
[06:39] Liam: ok scheduling — Noah proposed a 24h stability window starting 2025-07-15 00:00 UTC, is that still feasible for BlueAtlas?
[06:48] Maya: yes that works, we'll reserve the maintenance window and set staff oncall.
[06:52] Dan: security OK with that time.
[06:54] Noah: i'll create the calendar invite and link the runbook.
[06:58] Priya: measurement plan for the 24h run: baseline the same mixed-proxy workload at 120 qps with 400 qps spikes every 15m; capture p50/p95/p99, TLS handshake success rate, conntrack evictions, retransmit counts and route flaps. we'll provide the ingestion script to push traces to your S3.
[07:17] Raj: can you also provide a lightweight Prometheus scrape config for the metrics collector? we run a managed Prometheus so would prefer to keep scrapes minimal.
[07:24] Priya: will include a single endpoint job and example dashboard JSON.
[07:28] Liam: one last business item: fallback economics. we'll send a modeled example where 10% fallback over a week yields X in cost, including token breakdown and egress. is it OK to send as an attachment for procurement review?
[07:40] Dan: yes send to procurement and me.
[07:43] Liam: will do.
[07:45] Maya: any blockers from Redwood side for the 24h run?
[07:48] Priya: none — Redwood will pause kernel rollouts, provide MTU/NAT snippets, tracing commands, and the harness image.
[07:55] Liam: quick QA from earlier — where did you see the most conntrack evictions, transit gateway or on-prem edge?
[07:59] Elena: mostly on the on-prem firewall during the incident window.
[08:03] Priya: ok we'll add conntrack tuning flagged for on-prem firewall as well.
[08:07] Raj: sign off items: we'll share VPN logs and route tables from 07/07, and confirm ntp sync across hosts.
[08:14] Maya: yes thats our action.
[08:16] Liam: perfect. wrapping up — recap of next steps: 1) Redwood deliver MTU/NAT/iptables snippets + tracing commands (Priya), 2) Redwood share harness + runbook (Noah/Liam), 3) BlueAtlas share logs and route tables and confirm NTP (Maya/Raj), 4) Security confirm key rotation constraints (Dan). schedule 24h run 2025-07-15. any objections?
[08:40] Dan: none.
[08:42] Maya: good.
[08:44] Liam: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in thread and post the deliverables.
[08:49] END TRANSCRIPT

Notes: occasional transcription errors — some infra/tool names were autocorrected (e.g., 'conn track' -> 'con track', 'tcpdump' occasionally became 'tcp dump'). References: deliverables will be posted to shared Confluence and a private S3 link.
